info.title: DALI-2 IoT
info.description: *This API documentation is **work in progress**.In addition to the REST API, there is also a **websocket API** which provides asynchronous events for status updates etc. Documentation for this websocket API will be available soon.*

get.description: Get a list of all devices known to the Dali IoT

delete.description:
Delete all DALI devices on a specified DALI line.

If no DALI line is provided (default behaviour), all DALI devices will be deleted.

**Important**: Deleting the devices removes them from the application only.
This will not impact the configuration of the devices on the DALI bus.

get.description: *Get the information and features about a device*

delete.description:
*Delete the record of a single device*

**Important**: Does not change the configuration of the device

get.description:
Read the DALI Energy Reporting data for a device.

Some devices support only part of DALI Part 252, in which case the missing
values will be returned as null.

This will return the following errors:

- NOT FOUND (404), if the device does not exist.
- NOT IMPLEMENTED (501), if the device does not support DALI Part 252.
- INTERNAL SERVER ERROR (500), if reading the data fails.

Read out the Diagnostics and Maintenance Data for a device.

This will return the following errors:

- NOT FOUND (404), if the device does not exist.
- NOT IMPLEMENTED (501), if the device does not support DALI Part 253.
- INTERNAL SERVER ERROR (500), if reading the data fails.

Returns the last known scene values saved in the Display.

Last known scene values are silently updated when scene commands are
recognized on the DALI bus. The last known values can be wrong if scenes are
configured while the application is turned off or disconnected from the DALI
bus. Use POST /device/{_id}/scenes to query all scenes on the DALI bus.

The return value is an object with sub-objects for each scene number from 0
to 15. Each sub-object contains the scene values of supported features, such
as dimmable, colorRGB, colorWAF, colorKelvin, or colorXY. Unsupported
features are left out in the response. If a feature is supported, but the
scene is not configured, then `null` will be returned for this scene. `null`
will also be returned when a feature is partially supported, such as for the
channels amber (A) and free colour (F) in colorWAF of an RGBW dimmer.

get.description: Get the status of the currently active dali-scan.

post.description:
Start a new dali scan.

Note:
- If ``noAddressing`` is ``false`` and ``newInstallation`` is ``true`` a *new installation* is started:  all dali devices will be deleted prior to performing the scan, all devices will be addressed, already addressed devices will be re-addressed.
- If ``noAddressing`` is ``false`` and ``newInstallation`` is ``false`` a *system extension* is started: devices will be added to an existing system and new addresses will be added.
- If ``noAddressing`` is ``true`` a *current device list* scan is started: loads already addressed DALI bus and unaddressed devices remain unaddressed and will not be added.
- ``useLines`` can be used to only scan on a set of line numbers.
- If a scan is already active, this will not start a new one and answer with 409, because only one scan can run at any time. Call "/scan/cancel" if you want to start a new one.
Cancels a currently active scan.

get.description:
Checks the status on a line, with the following attributes:

- ``busVoltageDown`` if the line has power
- ``initializeMode`` if the line device is in initialization
- ``quiescentMode`` if quiescent mode has been activated for this line
- ``lineStatus`` string describing if the line is powered, unpowered or cant be communicated with

If lineStatus returns ``notReachable`` then all other info can be disregarded.
Returns a 404 error if the line was not found.

post.description:
Send 16-bit DALI frames (for DALI control gear) to a DALI bus.

Note that this request only handles up to 16 frames at once.
The address and command bytes take integers from 0 to 255.
For each requested frame, the response contains either an answer (integer from 0 to 255), or null, in order of the request frames.

Send 24-bit DALI frames (for DALI control devices) to a DALI bus.

Note that this request only handles up to 16 frames at once.
The address, instance and command bytes take integers from 0 to 255.
For each requested frame, the response contains either an answer (integer from 0 to 255), or null, in order of the request frames.

post.description:
Create a new event trigger action, which if enabled will start forwarding events.
Returns a 400 error if validation fails. The following things are checked:

- Source line is not a target line
- Filter pattern is possible for a Dali2 event frame
- Lines are known by the device (later deleted lines also disappear from the event trigger action)

static_fallback_retries.title: Static Fallback Retries
static_fallback_retries.description: The static fallback IP address 169.254.0.1/16 will be used if a DHCP server fails to assign an IP address within a 10s timeout. If retries is 0, then the static ip address will be used after a single 10s timeout. Otherwise, the device will retry for the specified amount of times; the total time is 10s x (1+static_fallback_retries). Retries must be 0 <= static_fallback_retries <= 60.

filters.title: Filters
filters.description:
Events are only forwarded if they match all the filters. This means that the event matches one listed entry for all categories.
For example an event with short address 1 and instance number 2 gets accepted by the filter "shortAddress: [1,2,3]", but would be rejected if a filter for instanceType gets added.
Leave empty to forward all event frames.
Filters with impossible combinations get rejected, possible combinations for two entries:

- shortAddress + instanceType
- shortAddress + instanceNumber
- deviceGroup + instanceType
- instanceType + instanceNumber
- deviceGroup + instanceType

tags.name: control
tags.description:
Endpoints to control devices
- **switchable**: *Turns the device on or off*
- **dimmable**: *Dims the device to a given percentage*
- **gotoLastActive**: *Turns the device on to it's last active level*
- **scene**: *Set the device to a given scene*
- **saveToScene**: *Store the current configuration to scene*
- **colorRGB**: *Set the device to a given RGB (red, green, blue) value from 0.0-1.0*
- **colorWAF**: *Set the device to a given WAF (white, amber, freecolour) value from 0.0-1.0*
- **colorKelvin**: *Set the device to a given color temperature in Kelvin*
- **colorXY**: *Set the device to a given XY color coordinate*

tags.name: zones
tags.description: Endpoints for managing zones. Zones may contain devices, other zones, DALI groups or DALI broadcasts; all of which can be controlled with a single request.
